why: A broad-range retailer making £50 million profit across 141 product lines (about £355,000 profit per product) is believable.
Pizza takeaway customers spending $36 to $78 over six months, falling as a rival opens nearby, is believable.
A laundry washing 2.4 to 3.1 million kg a month with about 32,000 to 48,000 paid hours (roughly 75 to 86 kg per working hour) at about $12 an hour is believable.
Repair costs of $27,600 for 157 faulty ovens (about $176, or under 6 technician hours at $31, per unit) and a $14,000 wiring contract are believable.
A 190-club chain with $277 to $292 million annual revenue (about $1.5 million per club) and a slowly falling margin is consistent with the revenue table and believable.
A fulfilment firm packing 1.4 to 1.9 million orders a week with 71,000 to 104,000 paid hours (about 18 to 22 orders per working hour) at $13 to $15 an hour is believable.
Film club subscribers spending $11 to $54 on tickets and snacks over six months, falling as streaming grows, is believable.
A health insurer handling about 620,000 claims a month with automatic settlement shares that fall stage by stage from 100% is believable.
A direct mattress seller with $16 to $45 million sales per area and advertising at roughly 5% to 13% of sales is believable.
A small tailor doing 41 alterations a month in 85 tailor hours and 187 in June in 425 hours (about two hours each) is believable.
